source.title: PrivUn: Unveiling Latent Ripple Effects and Shallow Forgetting in Privacy Unlearning
source.authors: Xiaoyi Chen; H. Wang; Si-Yuan Tang; Si-Jia Liu; Li-Ya Su; Xiao-Feng Wang; Hai-Xu Tang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates several established unlearning methods against direct retrieval, in-context recovery, and fine-tuning restoration, using a privacy-PII benchmark and its own recovery measures.
record.gate_note: Results cited from other papers about quantization, model tampering, and relearning are not recorded as this study's findings. The paper's CKA and association analyses are discussed, but do not establish the activation-ablation or access-blocking claim in version C. Table 1 and Table 2 contain many additional methods and conditions; selected results prioritize the versions tested and contrasts explicitly discussed in the text.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own direct-retrieval, ICL and fine-tuning recovery attacks on 19 unlearning methods (LLaMA-3.2-3B, GPT-2-Large) for PII forget sets. These results bear directly on A, B and E. Its own RAU method is tested against fine-tuning recovery, which bears on F.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that current methods look effective against direct retrieval but remain vulnerable to active ICL and especially fine-tuning recovery. They attribute this to gradient-driven ripple effects and shallow forgetting that leaves PII in intermediate layers. They propose association-aware core-set selection and RAU anchored at a mid layer (20), which lowers P3 to about 30% while keeping utility better than RMU.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates approximate unlearning on PII in Enron and TOFU, rather than the original knowledge-unlearning settings. It uses direct retrieval, ICL, and fine-tuning recovery measures and compares 19 methods; RAU is a proposed additional method.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery differs by unlearning method, known versus unknown set, forget-set proportion, dataset, and RAU intervention starting layer. The paper also reports different utility outcomes across LLaMA-3.2-3B and GPT-2-Large.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning a known subset also removes unknown-set PII (ripple effect). Forgetting score correlates with gradient association (Pearson 0.73), weakly with representation similarity (0.36), and not with the Enron social graph (−0.05).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning generalizes to non-targeted private data along gradient similarity rather than semantic or graph relations.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise CKA shows label-based methods change representations only near the output layers (NPO >0.98 until layer 24), while RMU changes mid-layers most (0.83 at layer 20).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods that resist fine-tuning recovery alter intermediate-layer representations; output-only changes leave recoverable information.

record.problems: Reported results are averages over 3 random seeds, but the presented text gives no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The principal evaluation uses PII datasets, limiting direct generalization to general knowledge unlearning. Many method and model results are tabulated but not all are extracted here; the paper also describes CKA curves without enough numeric layer-specific values in the text to catalog comprehensively.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 includes other methods and additional P1/P2/P3 and utility values across the 20% and 50% splits; Table 2 includes additional TOFU methods and attack metrics; Table 3 reports GPT-2-Large results. These were not individually extracted to prioritize direct P1/P2/P3 evidence for selected methods and the RAU layer comparison. Figure 3's CKA curves and other figure-only comparisons are also omitted because they do not directly measure activation ablation or demonstrate access-blocking rather than deletion.

untested.parts: Only PII forget sets (Enron, TOFU birth facts) are tested; there is no hazardous or general-knowledge benchmark (WMDP, Harry Potter) and no chance-level multiple-choice accuracy criterion.
The relearning set is 50 samples whose relation to the forget set is not stated. Unrelated vs loosely related relearning data is not varied, and general-knowledge recovery is not tested.
No activation-direction ablation. The CKA analysis shows where representations change but does not show retained-but-blocked knowledge.
No quantization experiments; quantization is only cited from Zhang et al. 2025.
Only few-shot ICL is tested; no rephrasing, jailbreaks or other languages.
RAU is tested only against P3 fine-tuning on LLaMA-3.2-3B Enron. No P1/P2, quantization, ablation or prompting attacks are reported for RAU, and RAU is not run on TOFU or GPT-2.

missing.what: RAU utility at layer 20 (QA 27.70, QA+ICL 35.41) vs RMU (8.35, 9.51). This is needed to judge whether the counter-method keeps general ability.
TOFU target and retrain baselines (P1 42.45%/0%, P2 47.64%/0%, P3 41.75%/2.13%) and DPO/RM/IDK P3 (32.14%, 35.71%, 27.38% on DFk).
GPT-2-Large: P1 0% for most methods but P3 up to 56%. The retrain P3 is 42.07%, close to the target's 46.72%, so P3 there barely exceeds the floor.
Target-model P1 (14.53%) and P2 (29.94%) baselines for the Enron rows, needed to read P1/P2 states.

record.verdict_notes: Double-linked P2 rows (A+E) and P3 rows (A+B) carry states that describe the recovery effect, so for A they read inversely (recovery observed = A fails). RAU rows were relinked to F only so their state can describe resistance. The P3 measure has a non-zero floor: the retrain model, never trained on the forget set, reaches 13.14% on LLaMA and 42.07% on GPT-2. So P3 partly measures learning from the 50 fine-tuning samples, and RMU's 16–20% is near that floor. The source of the 50 fine-tuning samples (forget-set subset or not) is not stated. Fine-tuning epochs differ by method (3e vs 10e). No error bars are reported. The setting is PII memorized via fine-tuning, not pretraining knowledge as in WMDP/Harry Potter.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures direct retrieval, active recovery, and utility for selected methods, but does not use the claim's near-chance accuracy criterion as a formal threshold or test all unlearning methods and settings.
Tests fine-tuning recovery on the study's PII data; does not test recovery of general knowledge or all small, unrelated, or loosely related relearning-set variants.
No activation-direction ablation; the representation analysis does not directly establish that the method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests in-context learning recovery, not rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or the full range of prompting-only attacks.
Tests the proposed RAU method against fine-tuning recovery across starting layers; does not test quantization, activation ablation, or prompting-only attacks.
